trajectory_messages.content:
I'd like to add an option to skip the up-front plugin pre-installation phase that the engine performs before a deployment.

*   The UpdateOptions struct must include a boolean field SkipPluginPreInstall (default false). When false, the engine performs the existing up-front pre-installation check by calling GetPluginPath on the PluginManager for every plugin the language host advertises as required, including packages that are imported but never used at runtime. When true, the engine skips this pre-installation traversal entirely.

*   When SkipPluginPreInstall is false, the engine must call GetPluginPath on the PluginManager for all plugins reported by the language host. For a program that advertises two packages (e.g. pkgA@1.0.0 and pkgB@1.0.0), GetPluginPath must be called for both, regardless of which packages are actually used at runtime.

*   When SkipPluginPreInstall is true, the engine must not call GetPluginPath for any plugins during the pre-installation phase. The set of plugins considered for up-front installation must be empty.

*   In both modes (SkipPluginPreInstall true or false), providers that are actually needed at runtime must still be loaded lazily by the provider registry when resources of that type are registered. A provider for a package that registers a resource must still be loaded exactly once; a provider for a package whose resources are never registered must not be loaded.

*   The TestUpdateOptions struct in the lifecycle test framework must expose a PluginManager field of type engine.PluginManager. When this field is non-nil, it must be used as the engine.Context.PluginManager for the test run. When nil, the engine context must default to using NopPluginManager{}.

77	// A tempFile is a wrapper around an *os.File that removes the underlying file when it is closed.
78	type tempFile struct {
79		f *os.File
80	}
81	
82	func (f tempFile) Read(b []byte) (int, error) {
83		return f.f.Read(b)
84	}
85	
86	func (f tempFile) Close() error {
87		closeErr := f.f.Close()
88		removeErr := os.Remove(f.f.Name())
89		return errors.Join(closeErr, removeErr)

128	// PluginSet represents a set of plugins.
129	type PluginSet map[string]workspace.PluginDescriptor
130	
131	// NewPluginSet creates a new PluginSet from the specified PluginSpecs.
132	func NewPluginSet(plugins ...workspace.PluginDescriptor) PluginSet {
133		var s PluginSet = make(map[string]workspace.PluginDescriptor, len(plugins))
134		for _, p := range plugins {
135			s.Add(p)
136		}
137		return s
138	}
139	
140	// Add adds a plugin to this plugin set.
141	func (p PluginSet) Add(plug workspace.PluginDescriptor) {
142		p[plug.String()] = plug
143	}
144	
145	// Removes less-specific entries.
146	//
147	// For example, the plugin aws would be removed if there was an already existing plugin aws-5.4.0.
148	func (p PluginSet) Deduplicate() PluginSet {
149		existing := map[string]workspace.PluginDescriptor{}
150		newSet := NewPluginSet()
151		add := func(p workspace.PluginDescriptor) {
152			prev, ok := existing[p.Name]
153			if ok {
154				// If either `pluginDownloadURL`, `Version` or both are set we consider the
155				// plugin fully specified and keep it. It is ok to keep `pkg v1.2.3` `pkg
156				// v2.3.4` and `pkg example.com` in a single set. What we don't want to do is
157				// keep `pkg` in that same set since there are more specific versions used. In
158				// general, there will be a `pky vX.Y.Y` in the plugin set because the user
159				// depended on a language package `pulumi-pkg` with version `x.y.z`.
160	
161				if p.Version == nil && p.PluginDownloadURL == "" {
162					// no new information
163					return
164				}
165	
166				if prev.Version == nil && prev.PluginDownloadURL == "" {
167					// New plugin is more specific then the old one
168					delete(newSet, prev.String())
169				}
170			}
171	
172			newSet.Add(p)
173			existing[p.Name] = p
174		}
175		for _, value := range p {
176			add(value)
177		}
178		return newSet
179	}
180	
181	// Values returns a slice of all of the plugins contained within this set.
182	func (p PluginSet) Values() []workspace.PluginDescriptor {
183		plugins := slice.Prealloc[workspace.PluginDescriptor](len(p))
184		for _, value := range p {
185			plugins = append(plugins, value)
186		}
187		return plugins
188	}

191	type PackageSet map[string]workspace.PackageDescriptor
192	
193	// NewPackageSet creates a new PackageSet from the specified PackageDescriptors.
194	func NewPackageSet(pkgs ...workspace.PackageDescriptor) PackageSet {
195		var s PackageSet = make(map[string]workspace.PackageDescriptor, len(pkgs))
196		for _, p := range pkgs {
197			s.Add(p)
198		}
199		return s
200	}
201	
202	// Add adds a package to this package set.
203	func (p PackageSet) Add(pkg workspace.PackageDescriptor) {
204		p[pkg.String()] = pkg
205	}
206	
207	// Union returns the union of this PackageSet with another PackageSet.
208	func (p PackageSet) Union(other PackageSet) PackageSet {
209		newSet := NewPackageSet()
210		for _, value := range p {
211			newSet.Add(value)
212		}
213		for _, value := range other {
214			newSet.Add(value)
215		}
216		return newSet
217	}
218	
219	// ToPluginSet converts this PackageSet to a PluginSet by discarding all parameterization information.
220	func (p PackageSet) ToPluginSet() PluginSet {
221		newSet := NewPluginSet()
222		for _, value := range p {
223			newSet.Add(value.PluginDescriptor)
224		}
225		return newSet
226	}
227	
228	// Values returns a slice of all of the packages contained within this set.
229	func (p PackageSet) Values() []workspace.PackageDescriptor {
230		pkgs := slice.Prealloc[workspace.PackageDescriptor](len(p))
231		for _, value := range p {
232			pkgs = append(pkgs, value)
233		}
234		return pkgs
235	}

443	func Update(u UpdateInfo, ctx *Context, opts UpdateOptions, dryRun bool) (
444		*deploy.Plan, display.ResourceChanges, error,
445	) {
446		contract.Requiref(ctx != nil, "ctx", "cannot be nil")
447		defer func() { ctx.Events <- NewCancelEvent() }()
448	
449		info, err := newDeploymentContext(ctx.Cancel.Base(), u, "update", ctx.ParentSpan)
450		if err != nil {
451			return nil, nil, err
452		}
453		defer info.Close()
454	
455		emitter, err := makeEventEmitter(ctx.Events, u)
456		if err != nil {
457			return nil, nil, err
458		}
459		defer emitter.Close()
460	
461		logging.V(7).Infof("*** Starting Update(preview=%v) ***", dryRun)
462		defer logging.V(7).Infof("*** Update(preview=%v) complete ***", dryRun)
463	
464		// We skip the target check here because the targeted resource may not exist yet.
465	
466		return update(ctx, info, &deploymentOptions{
467			UpdateOptions: opts,
468			SourceFunc:    newUpdateSource,
469			Events:        emitter,
470			Diag:          newEventSink(emitter, false),

477	func installPlugins(
478		ctx context.Context,
479		proj *workspace.Project, pwd, main string, target *deploy.Target, opts *deploymentOptions,
480		plugctx *plugin.Context, returnInstallErrors bool, manager *installManager,
481	) (PluginSet, map[tokens.Package]workspace.PackageDescriptor, error) {
482		// Before launching the source, ensure that we have all of the plugins that we need in order to proceed.
483		//
484		// There are two places that we need to look for plugins:
485		//   1. The language host, which reports to us the set of plugins that the program that's about to execute

## Summary

I implemented the `SkipPluginPreInstall` option to skip the engine's up-front plugin pre-installation phase.

### 1. `pkg/engine/update.go` — new `UpdateOptions` field
Added the `SkipPluginPreInstall bool` field to the `UpdateOptions` struct (default `false`).

### 2. `pkg/engine/update.go` — gated the pre-installation traversal in `installPlugins`
The set of plugins considered for up-front installation is now `preInstallPlugins`:
- When `SkipPluginPreInstall` is **false** (default): it's the full `allPlugins` set (every plugin reported by the language host + snapshot), so `ensurePluginsAreInstalled` → `GetPluginPath` runs for all of them, unchanged from before.
- When **true**: it's an empty `NewPluginSet()`, so `ensurePluginsAreInstalled` iterates nothing and `GetPluginPath` is never called during pre-installation.

Crucially, I left `computeDefaultProviderPackages` and the returned full `allPlugins` untouched, so in **both** modes the default-provider version mapping is still computed and providers are still loaded lazily by the provider registry when resources are actually registered.

### 3. `pkg/engine/lifecycletest/framework/framework.go` — `PluginManager` test field
- Added a `PluginManager engine.PluginManager` field to `TestUpdateOptions`.
- In `runWithContext`, the engine context now uses `opts.PluginManager` when non-nil, defaulting to `NopPluginManager{}` when nil.

The existing `NopPluginManager` struct already satisfies `engine.PluginManager` and is a plain empty struct, so it remains embeddable for test-specific managers that want to intercept/count `GetPluginPath` calls.

I did not touch anything under `tests/`. The `PluginManager` interface (`plugins.go`) already had the required `GetPluginPath` signature, so no interface change was needed.
